The [[1972 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XI Olympic Winter Games, was a winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Sapporo]], Japan, from 3 to 13 February 1972. A total of 1,006 athletes representing 35 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated in 35 events from 10 different [[Olympic sports|sports and disciplines]].<ref name="IOC">{{cite web|title=Sapporo 1972 Winter Olympics|url=http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Sapporo-1972/|work=Olympic.org|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=18 August 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100813073200/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Sapporo-1972/| archive-date= 13 August 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

Seventeen NOCs won at least one medal and fourteen of them collected at least one gold. The [[Soviet Union at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Soviet Union]] finished at the top of the gold and overall medal counts with 8 and 16, respectively. Along with [[Norway at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Norway]], the Soviet team also won the most silver medals (5). [[East Germany at the 1972 Winter Olympics|East Germany]], which ended the Games behind the Soviet Union with 14 medals, secured the most bronzes (7). The host nation, [[Japan at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Japan]], won a record total of three medals (one of each color), which included its first Winter Olympics gold medal.<ref name="modesto bee">{{cite news|title=Japan wins first gold medal; Schenk grabs 2nd|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=MRIuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=aH8FAAAAIBAJ&pg=916,1093738&dq=yukio+kasaya&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[The Modesto Bee]]|date=6 February 1972|agency=Associated Press|page=B-1}}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Three NOCs won a single medal: [[Canada at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Canada]] (silver), [[Poland at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Poland]] and [[Spain at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Spain]] (gold). For the last two, these were their first-ever gold medals at the Winter Olympics,<ref name="CBC sapporo">{{cite news|title=1972 Sapporo, Japan|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/1972-sapporo-japan-1.800516|work=Vancouver Now|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]|access-date=29 August 2010|date=18 December 2009|archive-date=23 November 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101123173655/http://www.cbc.ca/olympics/history/story/2009/11/26/sp-1972-sapporo.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and in the case of Spain, it was its first medal.<ref name="francisco ochoa">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Francisco Fernández Ochoa biography and Olympic results|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/fe/francisco-fernandez-ochoa-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418004830/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/fe/francisco-fernandez-ochoa-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 April 2020|access-date=29 August 2010}}</ref> This was Canada's weakest result since the [[1936 Winter Olympics]], when its athletes also brought home a single silver medal.<ref name="montreal gazette">{{cite news|title=Russian finish on top again|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=GpkuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=sqEFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2261,3589206&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[The Gazette (Montreal)|The Gazette]]|location=Montreal, Canada|date=14 February 1972|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020171741/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=GpkuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=sqEFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2261,3589206&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref>
The NOCs from the [[Republic of China at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Republic of China]] and the [[Philippines at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Philippines]] sent athletes to the Winter Olympics for the first time, but failed to win any medals.<ref name="TPE">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Chinese Taipei|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/TPE/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417093032/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/TPE/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|access-date=30 August 2010}}</ref><ref name="PHI">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Philippines|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/PHI/|access-date=30 August 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100813020004/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/PHI/| archive-date= 13 August 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref>

Hosting the Olympic Winter Games for the first time,<ref name="IOC" /> Japan's record consisted of a single medal: a silver in [[alpine skiing at the 1956 Winter Olympics]].<ref name="chiharu igaya">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Chiharu Igaya biography and Olympic results|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ig/chiharu-igaya-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417073527/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ig/chiharu-igaya-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|access-date=29 August 2010}}</ref> In Sapporo, [[Yukio Kasaya]], [[Akitsugu Konno]], and [[Seiji Aochi]] won the [[Ski jumping at the 1972 Winter Olympics|ski jumping]] normal hill (70&nbsp;m) gold, silver, and bronze medal, respectively. Kasaya's gold was Japan's first-ever at the Winter Games.<ref name="modesto bee" /> This result would persist as the country's best for the next 20 years.<ref name="JOC">{{cite web|title=Japanese delegation participation at the Olympic Games|url=http://www.joc.or.jp/english/aboutjoc/delegation.html|work=Japanese Olympic Committee|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]|access-date=29 August 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100806180156/http://www.joc.or.jp/english/aboutjoc/delegation.html| archive-date= 6 August 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

[[Wojciech Fortuna]] of Poland won the ski jumping's large hill (90&nbsp;m) event, while Spain's [[Francisco Fernández Ochoa]] prevailed in the [[Alpine skiing at the 1972 Winter Olympics|alpine skiing]]'s men's slalom, thus becoming their respective countries' first Winter Olympic champions.<ref name="CBC sapporo" /> Ochoa's gold medal was also Spain's first medal at the Winter Games.<ref name="francisco ochoa" /> [[Karen Magnussen]]'s silver in the [[Figure skating at the 1972 Winter Olympics|figure skating]] singles competition was Canada's sole medal and reflected what was the NOC's weakest performance since the 1936 Winter Games.<ref name="montreal gazette" />
For the first time in its history, a delegation from [[Finland at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Finland]] concluded its participation at the Winter Olympics without gold medals.<ref name="finland">{{cite web|title=1972 Sapporo|url=http://www.noc.fi/in_english/olympic_history/statistics_by_games/1972_sapporo/|work=Finnish Olympic Committee|publisher=[[Finnish Olympic Committee]]|access-date=29 August 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100215142333/http://www.noc.fi/in_english/olympic_history/statistics_by_games/1972_sapporo/|archive-date=15 February 2010}}</ref>

Six Soviet Union medals were won by two [[Cross-country skiing at the 1972 Winter Olympics|cross-country skiers]]: [[Galina Kulakova]], who took gold in both women's individual distances and in the relay event;<ref name="galina kulakova">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Galina Kulakova biography and Olympic results|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/galina-kulakova-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417111025/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ku/galina-kulakova-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|access-date=28 August 2010}}</ref> and [[Vyacheslav Vedenin]], who won the 30&nbsp;km—becoming the first Soviet skier to win an individual Olympic title—and the relay events, and came third in the 50&nbsp;km.<ref name="vyacheslav vedenin">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Vyacheslav Vedenin biography and Olympic results|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ve/vyacheslav-vedenin-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417161945/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ve/vyacheslav-vedenin-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|access-date=28 August 2010}}</ref> 
East German [[Luge at the 1972 Winter Olympics|lugers]] won eight medals for their NOC by taking every medal in the men's and women's singles, and placing two teams in the top three of the doubles event.<ref name="GDR luge">{{cite news|title=East Germany captures all luge singles|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=5wofAAAAIBAJ&sjid=GI0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=3573,1308513&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[Sarasota Journal]]|location=Sarasota, Florida|date=7 February 1972|agency=Associated Press|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020172130/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=5wofAAAAIBAJ&sjid=GI0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=3573,1308513&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="luge doubles">{{cite news|title=Both U.S. gold winners entered in 1,000 sprint|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=g9kvAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Su0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6821,3812994&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|location=Spokane, Washington|date=11 February 1972|agency=Associated Press|page=24|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020170839/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=g9kvAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Su0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6821,3812994&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> 
[[Paul Hildgartner]] and [[Walter Plaikner]] of [[Italy at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Italy]] were the only non-East German athletes to win a luge medal, as they shared the doubles gold with [[Horst Hörnlein]] and [[Reinhard Bredow]].<ref name="hildgartner-plaikner">{{cite news|last=Stevenson|first=Jack|title=Russians praise Henning|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=yyIRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=5YoDAAAAIBAJ&pg=7058,4543310&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[The Free Lance-Star]]|date=10 February 1972|agency=Associated Press|location=Fredericksburg, Virginia|page=8|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020172353/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=yyIRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=5YoDAAAAIBAJ&pg=7058,4543310&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> 
Italy's other gold medal was won by [[Gustav Thöni]] in the men's giant slalom;<ref name="gustav thoni">{{cite news|title=Italian wins giant slalom gold|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=F5kuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=sqEFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4972,4680615&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=The Gazette|date=10 February 1972|agency=Canadian Press/Associated Press/UPI|location=Montreal, Canada|page=26|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020174039/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=F5kuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=sqEFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4972,4680615&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> he also took silver in the men's slalom,<ref name="thoni silver">{{cite news|title=Olympics hail Spain|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=tdQMAAAAIBAJ&sjid=t2ADAAAAIBAJ&pg=5382,1801644&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[St. Petersburg Times]]|date=13 February 1972|agency=Associated Press|location=St. Petersburg, Florida}}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> thus contributing two of his country's five medals. 
[[Marie-Theres Nadig]] skied her way to victory in the women's downhill and giant slalom events,<ref name="marie theres nadig">{{cite news|last=Stevenson|first=Jack|title=Nadig wins 2nd event; U.S. fourth in skating|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=9ZgrAAAAIBAJ&sjid=sPUFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5424,1028887&hl=en|access-date=29 August 2010|newspaper=[[The Telegraph (Nashua)|The Telegraph]]|location=Nashua, New Hampshire|date=8 February 1972|agency=Associated Press|page=16|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020172130/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=9ZgrAAAAIBAJ&sjid=sPUFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5424,1028887&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> winning half of [[Switzerland at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Switzerland]]'s gold medals and helping her country achieve its best result at that time.{{ref|1|[n 1]}}
Two-time world figure skating champion [[Ondrej Nepela]] added the Olympic men's singles title to his career and guaranteed [[Czechoslovakia at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Czechoslovakia]]'s second and last gold medal in its Winter Olympics history.<ref name="ondrej nepela">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Ondrej Nepela biography and Olympic results|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ne/ondrej-nepela-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418005431/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ne/ondrej-nepela-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 April 2020|access-date=29 August 2010}}</ref>

Half of the [[United States at the 1972 Winter Olympics|United States]]' eight medals were obtained in women's [[Speed skating at the 1972 Winter Olympics|speed skating]]: [[Anne Henning]] won a gold in the 500&nbsp;m and a bronze in the 1000&nbsp;m, while [[Dianne Holum]] grabbed a gold in the 1500&nbsp;m and a silver in the 3000&nbsp;m.<ref name="henning-holum">{{cite news|title=Storybook finish for Winter Olympics|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=lwMdAAAAIBAJ&sjid=QJwEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3624,2414061&hl=en|access-date=3 October 2010|newspaper=[[The Tuscaloosa News]]|location=Tuscaloosa, Alabama|agency=Associated Press|date=14 February 1972|archive-date=20 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231020171741/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=lwMdAAAAIBAJ&sjid=QJwEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3624,2414061&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref> 
Also in this discipline, [[Ard Schenk]] (three golds), [[Stien Baas-Kaiser]] (one gold and one silver), [[Atje Keulen-Deelstra]] (one silver  and two bronzes), and [[Kees Verkerk]] (one silver) were responsible for all nine medals for the [[Netherlands at the 1972 Winter Olympics|Netherlands]].<ref name="Netherlands">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Netherlands speed skating at the 1972 Winter Olympics|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/NED/winter/1972/SSK/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417204044/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/NED/winter/1972/SSK/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|access-date=29 August 2010}}</ref> 
This was the best performance by a Dutch delegation at the Winter Olympics,{{ref|2|[n 2]}} and it took 26 years to be improved, when the Games [[1998 Winter Olympics|returned to Japan]].<ref name="NED">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Netherlands|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/NED/|access-date=29 August 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100728233038/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/NED/| archive-date= 28 July 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref>

==Medal table==
{{see also|List of 1972 Winter Olympics medal winners|Olympic medal table}}
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC convention in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC). The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next, and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=August 11, 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

In the doubles event in luge, two gold medals were awarded for a first place tie and, consequently, no silver medal was awarded.<ref name="luge doubles" /> This explains the 36 gold and 34 silver medals distributed during the Games.<ref name="IOC" />

==Notes==
#{{note|1|}} Switzerland also collected a total of 10 medals at the [[1948 Winter Olympics]] in St. Moritz, but it won only three golds versus the four obtained in Sapporo.<ref name="SUI">{{cite Sports-Reference|title=Switzerland|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SUI/|access-date=29 August 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100922121315/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/SUI/| archive-date= 22 September 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref>
#{{note|2|}} The Netherlands summed nine medals in Sapporo, just like at the [[1968 Winter Olympics]], but won four golds, one more than in Grenoble.<ref name="NED" />
